transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-01
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Jared (Redwood CSM), Elena (Sapphire - Head ML), Tom (Sapphire - Platform), Priya (Security), Marcus (CTO)

---
[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, quick intros, then go into network stuff and the onboarding runbook. um uh feel free to interrupt.
[00:00:20] Elena: hi all, elena here. excited to get this rolling. our primary use case is customer-facing summarization and internal search embeddings.
[00:00:35] Marcus: Marcus, CTO. timeline's tight — pilot in 6 weeks if possible.
[00:00:42] Tom: Tom, I'll handle networking and infra.
[00:00:47] Priya: Priya, security lead — I'll be checking compliance and KMS questions.
[00:00:52] Maya: great, thanks. Connor and Jared from our side as well. Connor will walk the architecture; Jared will handle security artifacts and the onboarding runbook.

[00:01:20] Connor: thanks. quick topo, Redwood provides hosted inference or private VPC installs. For an enterprise like you we recommend Private (VPC) so keys never leave, and we can pin model versions. but we can do hosted for faster start if wanted.
[00:01:45] Tom: we prefer VPC-hosted, yes. what does the peering look like — do you need inbound or outbound? our security team is strict on inbound.
[00:01:58] Connor: primarily outbound from your VPC to our control plane on 443, and we do a peered data-plane path for model traffic when using Redwood Private; that can be configured as a private link. firewall wise, allow egress to the Redwood control IPs — we'll send a CIDR list.

[00:02:35] Priya: is data encrypted in transit and at rest? KMS integration?
[00:02:42] Jared: yes, at rest is encrypted; for Private we integrate with customer KMS via our KMS adapter — note, sometimes the transcript calls it "customer KMS plug" or something, it's the KMS adaptor. we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via KMIP. we'll share the integration doc.
[00:03:03] Priya: ok, need the architecture diagram + key rotation schedule.

[00:03:25] Connor: on performance — we suggested a quantized model for lower cost, but you'll want to validate p99 latency. Batching helps cost but increases latency; we can set continuous batching with a 30ms target or keep per-request low-latency paths.
[00:03:50] Elena: baseline latency target is <200ms p95 for short prompts, and we need embeddings under 150ms if possible.
[00:03:58] Connor: noted; we'll run a perf test tuned to sample prompt set. I'll include KV cache hit ratio expectations — that helps a lot for conversational workloads.

[00:04:25] Maya: timeline check — Marcus said 6 weeks to pilot. is that realistic?
[00:04:31] Marcus: yes, pilot with limited set of users and model endpoints.
[00:04:36] Tom: we need a staging runbook and a rollback plan. who owns rollback?
[00:04:41] Jared: Redwood provides rollouts: canary, A/B, and auto-fallback to prior model. we'll include the rollback steps in the runbook.

[00:05:10] Elena: question about logs and audit — we need per-request audit logs for up to 90 days and token-level cost breakout for our finance team.
[00:05:19] Jared: we capture request traces and token counts; on Private you can ship logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog); we'll share sample dashboards.

[00:05:45] Speaker 7 (automated note): Action item noted: send runbook.

[00:06:05] Tom: on egress, do we have to allow ports for GPU hosts? sometimes vendors ask for port ranges.
[00:06:12] Connor: no special ports — everything is over TLS 443. but for private data plane we may request peering/VPC endpoints. we'll outline exact network flows in the diagram.

[00:06:40] Priya: what about SOC 2 and ISO artifacts? we need evidence for our audit in Q4.
[00:06:46] Jared: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs; I'll attach the certs and the third-party pen test summary. also note SSO: we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:07:05] Priya: SCIM is a must. Ok.

[00:07:30] Elena: can we talk about model pinning and rollout — we can't have silent quality regressions.
[00:07:36] Connor: absolutely. you can pin a model version to a route and have a canary percentage. we also support eval hooks to compare outputs against a golden prompt set; if quality degrades beyond thresholds we can auto-fallback. sometimes the transcript writes "golden set" as "golden net" — just clarifying.

[00:08:10] Marcus: does Redwood provide cost estimations per 1000 requests? finance will want a sense of unit economics.
[00:08:18] Maya: yes we provide token-level cost analytics and Redwood Optimize suggestions. we'll send a cost estimator and example billing for projected volume.

[00:08:45] Elena: any special compliance for embeddings storage? our embeddings database will be internal only.
[00:08:51] Jared: for Private, embeddings never leave your VPC unless you opt in. For hosted, we do short-term caching with options to disable. we'll include the retention settings in the runbook.

[00:09:20] Tom: what's the onboarding cadence? weekly check-ins?
[00:09:24] Maya: typical cadence is twice-weekly for the first two weeks, then weekly. Jared will lead security calls.

[00:09:40] Connor: technical deep-dive we'll need sample prompts, sample concurrency numbers, and sequence length distributions — that informs kernel selection and batching.
[00:09:53] Elena: i'll send a 20-example prompt set and a 5000-line synthetic trace of expected load.

[00:10:10] Marcus: any gotchas with our bank-grade network? we use strict egress and NAT gateways.
[00:10:16] Connor: NAT is fine. we may ask for static egress IPs for allowlisting; if NAT changes frequently that complicates allowlisting.

[00:10:35] Priya: encryption keys: can we rotate without downtime?
[00:10:40] Jared: yes, key rotation is supported; we'll document the rotation window and recommended steps.

[00:11:00] Maya: okay let's walk through the runbook outline — Jared, you want to narrate?
[00:11:05] Jared: sure. section one: access and identity (SSO, SCIM, RBAC), section two: network and peering, section three: deployment patterns (canary, A/B), section four: observability and dashboards, section five: security artifacts and compliance, section six: pilot checklist and sign-off.

[00:11:34] Elena: for RBAC we need role separation: dev vs prod admin, and a read-only analytics role — can Redwood map to our AD groups?
[00:11:42] Jared: we map SAML assertions to RBAC roles and support group sync via SCIM.

[00:12:05] Tom: how long to provision the Private data plane once network is ready?
[00:12:09] Connor: once peering and CIDRs are shared, we typically provision in 2-3 days for staging; production can be scheduled and takes 3-5 business days depending on capacity.

[00:12:30] Marcus: any need for on-prem hardware? we prefer cloud but want future-proofing.
[00:12:35] Connor: Redwood Private supports on-prem options; we'd scope separately. for now cloud VPC is sufficient.

[00:12:55] Elena: what's the fallback if a model update breaks outputs? how quickly can we roll back?
[00:13:00] Connor: with canary+auto-fallback you can revert within minutes; manual rollback is immediate for pinned routes.

[00:13:20] Maya: let's capture success criteria for the pilot: 1) 500 users on staging with <200ms p95 on summarization, 2) embeddings integrated into search with latency <150ms p95, 3) SOC2 artifacts received and KMS configured. agree?
[00:13:36] Elena: yes.
[00:13:38] Marcus: yes.

[00:13:50] Tom: one operational question: what metrics are surfaced to our dashboards? token usage, latency percentiles, error rates?
[00:13:57] Jared: token usage, per-route latency p50/p95/p99, error counts, batch sizes, cache hit rates, and rollout statuses. we'll provide a sample Grafana dashboard.

[00:14:25] Connor: note on perf testing — we recommend a 30-minute steady-state run at expected concurrency and a spike test. for embeddings, we'll run microbenchmarks per model variant.

[00:14:43] Elena: also want quality regression alerts tied to the golden prompt set.
[00:14:47] Connor: yes, we'll configure eval alerts; if the BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies drop below threshold we trigger an alert. sometimes the MLE folks call it "rouge-ish" in notes.

[00:15:10] Maya: ok, logistics: i'll send calendar invites for the runbook walkthrough and the VPC walkthrough. preferred times?
[00:15:16] Tom: mornings PST are best.

[00:15:30] Maya: noted. Jared will share the doc bundle after this call.

[00:15:45] [00:30:00] (middle of call — deep technical Q&A)
[00:30:05] Tom: concurrency — we expect bursts to 200 qps for embeddings during nightly batch jobs, but average is 20 qps. what kind of autoscaling behavior should we expect?
[00:30:14] Connor: Dedicated pools can autoscale with warm pools for bursts. with private you can configure burst capacity and a gracefully-degrading policy. important to set target utilization; we typically recommend 60-70% to avoid queuing.

[00:30:46] Priya: on data residency — can logs be kept in eu-west only? we have a subsidiary in EU.
[00:30:52] Jared: yes, region pinning is possible for data-plane resources. we'll call this out in the deployment settings.

[00:31:10] Elena: curious about model quantization quality — our legal team worries about hallucinations; will quantization impact answer quality?
[00:31:18] Connor: some small drop possible depending on model and task. we'll recommend a quantization profile and run quality regressions on the golden prompt set. you can opt for mixed precision if you want better quality with some cost tradeoff.

[00:31:46] Marcus: who signs off on production readiness at your side?
[00:31:50] Jared: CSM plus an infra owner; we do a joint checklist sign-off with customer ops and security.

[00:32:15] Maya: ok, last section: documentation links and shared artifacts. we'll post: onboarding runbook, network diagram template, sample perf script, SOC2 pack, KMS guide, cost estimator spreadsheet.
[00:32:30] Elena: perfect. can you also include sample prompts annotated with expected outputs?
[00:32:36] Connor: yes.

[00:33:00] Tom: one more — will we get a staging API key or do we need to go through SSO first?
[00:33:06] Jared: we'll provide staging API keys and a short-lived token flow; for production we'll require SSO/SCIM.

[00:33:25] Maya: wrap-up: recap next steps and action items. Connor will own perf plan; Jared security docs; Maya commercial checklist and scheduling; Tom to provide network details.
[00:33:40] Marcus: sounds good.

[00:33:50] Priya: thanks all.
[00:33:55] Elena: thanks. excited to start.

[00:34:00] Maya: meeting end. We'll follow up with the bundle within 48 hours.

---
Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (product names, acronyms) and generic speaker tags where the recorder wasn't confident. Some timestamps approximate.
